body:
her answer to years of being picked apart was a song you can do a bad dance to. she’d answered critics before from a victimized perspective; this one shrugs. august 18, 2014: it entered the hot 100 at no. 1, the 22nd ever to do it.

why: Calendar slot 2026-08-18 15:00Z X, heartbeat:on-this-day, hook "the contradiction". Genuine dated Vault match: the 1989 item "Shake It Off, and the pivot from victim to punchline-maker" (2014-08-18, sourced Wikipedia + Rolling Stone). Claims used: her Rolling Stone framing that "Mean" had answered critics "from kind of a victimized perspective" and that the new response was to get good at dodging punches; the song dropping the same day as the album-announcement livestream; and entering the Hot 100 at No. 1 as only the 22nd song ever to debut on top. Kept clear of the 08-13 Decode post, which uses the same date only as a clue payoff, and of the 08-15 "Mean" track-fact — "Mean" is not named here. Trimmed to weighted ≤270 per X length rule.
